sections.title: CNS Protection and Routes of Infection

content.text: The CNS is protected by multiple physical and physiological barriers: the bony skull and vertebral column, the dura mater, and the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Notably, the brain lacks a conventional lymphatic drainage system. Pathogens can reach the CNS through hematogenous spread (most common), direct extension from adjacent infected structures (sinus, mastoid), or penetrating trauma. When infection establishes, it can involve brain parenchyma (cerebritis, abscess, encephalitis), extra-axial spaces (subdural empyema, epidural abscess), or meninges (meningitis).
Hematogen (paling sering)
Ekstensi langsung dari sinus/mastoid
Trauma penetrasi

sections.title: Cerebritis dan Formasi Kapsul

content.text: CEREBRITIS (7-10 days): The initial stage of pyogenic infection marked by edema with flattened gyri. Lesions may be bilateral in temporal and frontal regions depending on the area affected. CAPSULE FORMATION (10-14 days): As the infection matures, necrosis, debris, and pus accumulate in a central cavity. Granulation tissue and fibrocollagenous thickening form the abscess wall. Reactive astrocytosis, neovascularity, and vasogenic edema develop around the abscess. Blood supply becomes 3-5 times greater in gray matter compared to white matter in the affected area. Otogenic abscesses typically occur in the temporal lobe; rhinogenic abscesses in the frontal lobe.
Cerebritis: stadium awal infeksi piogenik (7-10 hari), edema, gyri mendatar
Capsul formasi: 10-14 hari setelah inokulasi, nekrosis, debris, pus
Granulasi dan penebalan dinding fibrokologen
Otogenik abses: lobus temporal; Rinogenik abses: lobus frontal
Temporal evolution is key: cerebritis 7-10 days, capsule formation begins at 10-14 days

sections.title: Ensefalitis - CT dan MRI

content.text: Encephalitis is typically viral, causing acute, subacute, or chronic parenchymal inflammation. CT findings include vasogenic edema, mass effect, and heterogeneous enhancement with variable degrees. In later phases, mild hemorrhage may be visible. MRI is the modality of choice. T1W shows edema in affected areas; if complex with subacute hemorrhage, hyperintense areas may be seen. T1 C+ (gadolinium): enhancement is typically absent in early cases; in advanced cases, patterns include gyral enhancement, leptomeningeal enhancement, ring enhancement, and diffuse enhancement. T2W shows hyperintensity in white matter and cortex; hemorrhagic components appear hyperintense. DWI/ADC is more sensitive than T2WI - restricted diffusion occurs due to cytotoxic edema but is less intense than infarction. T2 shine-through can occur from vasogenic edema. GRE/SWI can demonstrate active hemorrhage (rare in neonates, common in older patients).
CT: vasogenic edema, efek massa, penyangatan heterogen
MRI T1: edema area terkena; T1 C+: gyral, leptomeningeal, ring, atau diffuse enhancement
MRI T2: hyperintensity white matter dan cortex
DWI/ADC: restricted diffusion (cytotoxic edema), lebih sensitif dari T2WI
GRE/SWI: dapat menunjukkan perdarahan aktif
DWI is more sensitive than T2 for early encephalitis; restricted diffusion from cytotoxic edema

sections.title: Meningitis dan Empyema

content.text: MENINGITIS: Acute purulent meningitis shows exudate in the subarachnoid space, congested subarachnoid vessels, and brain swelling. Chronic forms are often due to TB or Cryptococcus. Complications include communicating hydrocephalus, ventriculitis, and dural vein thrombosis leading to infarction. EMPYEMA: Accumulation of inflammatory debris in the subdural space (rarely epidural).
Meningitis akut: eksudat di subarachnoid space, pembuluh darah kongesti, otak membengkak
Kronik: sering TB atau Kriptokokus
Komplikasi: hidrosefalus komunikan, ventrikulitis, trombosis vena dural
Empyema: akumulasi debris inflamasi di subdural

sections.title: TB CNS dan Toksoplasmosis

content.text: TB CNS manifests in two forms: meningeal inflammation (70-80% of cases) and tuberculoma formation (20-30%). Tuberculomas may present as abscesses, though this is rare. TOXOPLASMOSIS: CT shows multiple hypodense lesions with calcifications. With contrast: nodules and ring enhancement. MRI shows multiple ring-enhancing lesions on T2W.
TB CNS: proses inflamasi meningeal 70-80%, tuberkuloma 20-30%
Toksoplasmosis: multiple ring-enhancing lesions

diagnostic_logic.title: Identify anatomical compartment
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Parenchyma vs meninges vs extra-axial space

diagnostic_logic.title: Characterize enhancement pattern
diagnostic_logic.explanation: Gyral, leptomeningeal, ring, or diffuse enhancement provides diagnostic clues

diagnostic_logic.title: Use advanced MRI sequences
diagnostic_logic.explanation: DWI for cytotoxic edema, GRE/SWI for hemorrhage

differential_notes.how_to_separate: DWI: both show restricted diffusion but encephalitis less intense; clinical context differs
Tuberculoma: often single, basal location; Toxoplasmosis: multiple, ring-enhancing, immunocompromised patient
Bacterial: purulent exudate, more pronounced enhancement; Viral: milder meningeal changes

red_flags: Abscess with mass effect or ventricular proximity
